open_points.subject: flow:owner_sign_in_and_session — session cookie on loopback HTTP
open_points.text: “Registry always marks it HTTPS-only” and “a browser on Registry's own machine accepts it from a loopback address over plain HTTP”
open_points.question: Must a session cookie work over plain HTTP on every supported loopback address, and if so, what cookie setting guarantees that while it is always marked HTTPS-only?
options: Always set the Secure attribute and require supported browsers to send it on loopback HTTP
Do not set the Secure attribute for loopback HTTP
open_points.default_guess: Always set the Secure attribute and require HTTPS on loopback as well.

witness.initial: Registry's owner interface is configured at http://127.0.0.1 and no owner session exists.
events: The owner signs in from a browser on Registry's machine.
module:owner_interface returns the session cookie marked HTTPS-only.
The browser makes the next owner request over the same plain-HTTP loopback origin.
outcomes: The browser accepts and sends the cookie, so the session request is admitted.
The browser does not send the HTTPS-only cookie over HTTP, so the request is treated as having no valid session.

open_points.subject: flow:import_from_vps — outputs of upload framing
open_points.text: “capability:upload_framing.read_upload_head … answers its CSRF value” while module:owner_interface later hands on “its declared length … and an unread stream that ends where the part ends”
open_points.question: Which offered capability creates and returns the file-part stream and its derived declared length, and is that part of read_upload_head's result?
options: read_upload_head returns the CSRF value, derived file length and lazy file stream together
Add a separate upload_framing capability that returns the framed file part
Have owner_interface construct the file stream and length itself
open_points.default_guess: Make read_upload_head return all three values together.

open_points.subject: flow:import_from_vps — invalid multipart head
open_points.text: “answers its CSRF value, or none for a head of another form”
open_points.question: What exact outcome does read_upload_head produce for truncated input, malformed multipart syntax, a missing second part, invalid file-part headers, or an I/O failure while reading the bounded head?
options: Treat every such case as no CSRF and let the session check refuse it
Treat transport I/O failure as an internal operation failure
open_points.default_guess: Return a distinct malformed-upload refusal, with no file byte retained or parsed.

witness.initial: A valid owner session submits an upload whose first CSRF part is valid but whose second part has truncated headers.
events: module:upload_framing reads the bounded multipart head.
The parser reaches the malformed second-part headers.
outcomes: It answers no CSRF, and module:owner_sessions reports the ordinary stage-(1) CSRF refusal.
It reports a malformed or unreadable upload, preserving the distinction from a wrong CSRF value.

open_points.subject: context — derivation of the file part's declared length
open_points.text: “the request's declared length less the head it read and the closing delimiter with its final `--` and line end”
open_points.question: What is the result when the request's declared length is smaller than the parsed head plus the required closing delimiter, does not match the bytes delivered by the transport, or the closing delimiter is missing or malformed?
options: Return no declared file length and continue counting actual file bytes
Refuse the upload as malformed before reading file bytes
Clamp the derived length to zero
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the upload as malformed before reading any file-part byte.

witness.initial: A valid session sends a syntactically valid bounded head but declares a body length smaller than the head plus the required closing delimiter.
events: module:upload_framing parses the CSRF part and file headers.
It attempts to derive the file part's declared length by subtraction.
outcomes: The derived length is treated as absent and migration_import reads and counts the stream.
The request is refused as malformed before migration_import reads the file stream.

open_points.subject: flow:daily_backup — provider and caller of the backup location
open_points.text: “capability:backups.newest_backup_instant … in the backup location capability:configuration.give_backup_location gives” while operations says the backup location is “asked by operations when an action needs” it and backups itself knows configuration
open_points.question: Who calls give_backup_location for this read, and who passes the location to newest_backup_instant?
options: operations obtains the location and passes it to backups
backups obtains the location directly from configuration
owner_interface obtains the location before calling operations
open_points.default_guess: operations obtains the location and passes it to backups.
